⭐ Disappointing Service – Poor Communication and Lack of Accountability

I’m extremely disappointed with my experience at Five Lands Veterinary. I was made to attend an appointment based on incorrect information, as the appointment date I was given did not match the date stated in the text message. This resulted in an unnecessary journey and a complete waste of my time.

What makes this even more frustrating is the double standard. If a customer arrives late for an appointment, they can face a charge. Yet when the practice makes a mistake that inconveniences the customer, all you receive is an apology. Customers are expected to respect appointment times and follow the rules, so surely the same level of accountability should apply to the practice itself.

What makes this particularly disappointing is that Five Lands Veterinary is one of the pricier veterinary practices, and you would naturally expect a higher standard of service, communication and professionalism when paying those prices. Unfortunately, my experience has not reflected that expectation.

This is not the first time my family has had concerns either. When I was younger, my older sister also experienced issues with the service provided by Five Lands Veterinary regarding my cat. To now experience problems myself, years later, is disappointing and raises questions about whether enough has been done to improve the customer experience.

Most importantly, my dog, Luna, was the one caught up in all this confusion. She was understandably confused by the unnecessary trip, and it was frustrating to put her through that experience because of an appointment date mix-up that could have been avoided with proper communication.

I understand that mistakes can happen, but customers' time is valuable too. An apology does not undo the inconvenience caused. When customers are expected to pay fees for lateness, it seems only fair that the practice should take greater responsibility when its own errors waste people's time.

Unfortunately, this experience has been the final straw, and I will be moving Luna to another veterinary practice. Given the prices charged, I expected much better service, communication and accountability. I no longer feel that Five Lands Veterinary offers the level of customer care I expect for both myself and my dog.

I hope management takes this feedback seriously and improves its appointment management and customer service so that other pet owners do not have to experience the same frustration.

Consultations are extremely expensive for what feels like a very minimal examination. In most cases the vet briefly checks the cat’s weight and glances at their eyes, but there is very little effort made to properly investigate symptoms or listen to concerns. It often feels like the focus is on treating surface-level symptoms rather than attempting to diagnose the underlying cause.

Medication is hugely overpriced. On multiple occasions I have been prescribed medication that costs double the price compared to buying the exact same medication online. This seems to be the case with almost every prescription.

The “Wellness Screen” in particular felt very misleading. It’s advertised as a £89 full health check or medical MOT but in practice it did not resemble a comprehensive check at all. Many of the items listed as part of the check were either not done properly or not done at all:

• Weight and joints check: only her weight was checked; her joints were not examined.
• Teeth and gums inspection: these were not looked at - the nurse simply referred to a note in her records.
• Eyes, ears, skin, and coat exam: her coat was barely looked at and only after I prompted it.
• Joint and mobility assessment: no physical check was done,  I was simply asked about how exercise. Just how is she with excercise, not how often does she exercise, no follow up questions about whether she struggles given her age.
• Parasite protection review: I was asked when I last treated for fleas and the cat was briefly combed. No questions about worming. Didn't ask what I use to worm her. No advice or follow up questions.
• Nutrition and preventative care advice: no advice was given. Nutrition wasn't acknowledged at all. Just asked what type of cat food and when I said wet there was no follow up questions about the brand etc.
• Vaccination check: I was asked if vaccinations were up to date with no further discussion or guidance.

Blood tests were also presented as part of the wellness screen, but unless your cat is completely placid, they apparently cannot take blood without significant difficulty. We were sent home with anxiety medication because they could not take the blood sample. If your cat continues to resist you will be slapped with a £300 to sedate them which begs the question of whether the staff have received sufficient training to do blood tests. And why take from the neck rather than other areas of the body which may be less distressing, such as the back leg? Overall, the “comprehensive health check” claim feel quite misleading. It was as lacklustre as the usual £70 consultations. And please be aware that once the results come in you will be booked in for another £70 consultation to discuss the outcomes with a vet. So you'll find the £89 wellness screen quickly becomes £190 with anxiety meds and follow up consultation but can go up to £490 if your cat needs to be sedated!

Another concern is the overall culture in the clinic. While waiting, I have on many occasions overheard reception staff openly gossiping about clients, which creates a very uncomfortable and unprofessional atmosphere.

It also often feels like there is constant pressure to add additional procedures and costs. I’ve heard many similar experiences from friends and family who also attend this clinic. A simple visit can quickly escalate blood tests, then sedation because the cat is “too stressed”, then xrays and before you know it you are facing a bill of £1000+ which would be fine if you left with a clear diagnosis but I find that that is rarely the case.

Wait times are also frustrating. I have waited 15+ minutes past my appointment time, yet if a client were that late they would likely be charged a missed appointment fee.

To be fair, there are a few staff members who have been excellent. Zoe and Anzal have both been thorough and considerate of treatment costs, and Poppy is also very kind and helpful. Unfortunately, they seem to be the exception rather than the rule.

My last visit was very bad and upsetting.
I been a loyal customer with Fivelands Vets since my dog was puppy.  Seems like there is no loyalty provided back. Bills are extortionate for a simple visits!
This one star is for last visit and for the feeling that noone looks out for you there anymore!
Over many years visits were ok , some Vets nicer than others but generally everything was fine. Ladies at the front are always nice but could greet you with a bigger smile.
Lately, every time I see a new face Vets , which is not nice, as it feels they are not familiar with me or my dog.
So this time Vet was a young lady with black hair. I felt she didn't greet my dog like some Vets do. She picked a huge muzzle at first, when I said that's too big, she took a smaller one. ( she should have known from the size of the dog). My dog needed to check the ear as it has a dark brown discharge inside. Once she looked, she started to talk about the inner growing hair, which I know about, but my worry is a dark brown discharge as it says on google and anywhere you look that it most likely is to do with an ear infection.  I felt that she didn't listen to other comments I made about how my dog behaves with this issue. She prescribed medicine,  which was what I came for.
I mentioned on the phone when booked that I will want to do a nail clipping as well. Vet clearly didn't want to do it. I had to ask, She said:" it should be ok if she exercises enough , doesn't look too long and glancet at the dog who stood on the ground " ! Really? It never has been a case that my dogs nails would get short enough,  we don't walk many hours each day and she is getting old and slow. The inner nails were already long and bendy. That's not even a point, I asked, you take a good look at my dog! She clipped the nails after I said it's been few months since it was done.
Then I place my dog on the floor and told
the Vet  that my dog have lumps on the chest. I asked if she can place her hand on my dogs chest to see what she thinks!? She looked very uninterested  saying that she sees it on the records and that she would have to muzzle dog again!  Seriously!? This is the part where I could scream! If anything ,  I would expect her to look at the records and to ask me how my dogs chest is and to be willing to look.  If she was any dog person, she knows she could have stroked my dog and touched the chest. Noone ever put muzzle on my dog to touch her and to check her health. This time there was no routine check either ( listening to heart, checking tummy) , but the bill was if some sort of magic examination was performed!
So I go out, already upset, to get the bill. Lady behing a counter mentiones £130 but on the card machine shows £170.
So she goes and double checks, comes back and said that the Vet has put nail clipping on, at price £36!!!!!!!
I ask what's includen in the consultation then?

On the bill £170 = 1 bag of dry dog food £15.50,  consultation ( repeated) £65.50,  ear medicine  £45.87!!!, dewormer tablet £8.72, nail clipping, £36. How does it sounds to you all?, I think it's a little steep!  Even ear medicine ,  since when is that so expensive !?

So I ask to speak to manager.
Manager explains that the vet charged me as for repeated consultation and the nail clipping on top. If she charged as new consultation,  it will be cheaper! Then I am asked if I WANT Them to look at altering the bill!  Seriously? This is the point when I believe they should be looking out for me and to alter it immediately or shouldn't have tried to overcharge at first place!
So the manager edits the bill by changing consultation to full fee £72.50 , which includes nails and bill drops to £142 ( so called repeated visit was £7 punds cheaper, what a joke).
Almost £30 punds, just like that!
Do these vets care about any customers?

So I am very upset of this visit, and I will never forgive that Vet for not  checking my dogs lumps on the chest! I thought Vets are supposed to do all they can to help animals!
